sources.title: Batch 0059 frozen Spring circular-dependency source context

claims.text: The four frozen source Questions ask how Spring resolves Bean/singleton-Bean circular dependencies and are currently classified as a mechanism answer; the answer must explain lifecycle and registry mechanics rather than invent a project scenario.

Supported singleton circular references can be broken by exposing an early reference after instantiation and before full dependency population/initialization, while constructor-to-constructor cycles remain unresolvable because no instance is available for early exposure.

The interview shorthand three-level cache maps to singletonObjects for final singletons, earlySingletonObjects for materialized early references, and singletonFactories for lazy early-reference factories; a factory is registered before dependency population and can be materialized by getSingleton when the bean is currently in creation.

The lazy factory can delegate through getEarlyBeanReference and SmartInstantiationAwareBeanPostProcessor so an early dependency can receive a wrapped/proxy reference when required; Spring also guards against inconsistent raw early injection when the final bean is wrapped.

The early-exposure path is conditioned by singleton scope, the bean being currently in creation, and circular-reference policy such as allowCircularReferences; it must not be generalized to prototype beans or arbitrary object-graph cycles.
